title.raw: 卷一百二十五 志第七十八 禮二十八 Volume 125 Treatises 78: Rites 28

sentences.zh: 禮二十八

translations.literal: Rites 28
translations.idiomatic: Rites 28

sentences.zh: 〈（凶禮四）〉

translations.literal: (Mourning Rites IV)
translations.idiomatic: Mourning Rites IV)

sentences.zh: ○士庶人喪禮服紀

translations.literal: ○ Regulations on Funeral Rites and Mourning Garb for Gentry and Commoners
translations.idiomatic: Funeral Rites and Mourning Garb for Gentry and Commoners

sentences.zh: 士庶人喪禮。

translations.literal: Funeral rites for gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites for the gentry and commoners.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年十月，詔開封府：禁喪葬之家不得用道、釋威儀及裝束異色人物前引。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaibao, an edict was issued to the Kaifeng prefectural government: households conducting funerals were forbidden to employ Daoist or Buddhist ceremonial displays, or to have figures in outlandish dress and colors lead the procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kaibao 3 (970), the court ordered the Kaifeng prefecture to bar funeral households from using Daoist or Buddhist ritual pageantry or from having bizarrely costumed figures lead the cortege.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七 年正月，命翰林學士李昉等重定士庶喪葬制度。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, Academician-Expositor Li Fang and others were ordered to redraw the regulations on funerals for gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taiping Xingguo 7 (982), Li Fang of the Hanlin Academy and his colleagues were commissioned to revise the funeral code for gentry and commoners.

sentences.zh: 昉等奏議曰：「唐大曆七年，詔喪葬之家送葬祭盤，隻得於喪家及塋所置祭，不得於街衢張設。

translations.literal: Fang and the others submitted a memorial stating: "In the seventh year of Dali of Tang, an edict provided that funeral households setting out offering trays for the burial procession might set up sacrifices only at the bereaved home and at the grave site, and might not set them up along the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his colleagues proposed: "Under Tang Dali 7 (772), funeral households were told that burial offering trays could be set up only at the mourners' home and at the cemetery, not in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 又長慶三年，令百姓 喪葬祭奠不得以金銀、錦繡為飾及陳設音樂，葬物稍涉僭越，並勒毀除。

translations.literal: Again, in the third year of Changqing, common people were ordered that in funeral sacrifices they might not use gold, silver, or brocade as ornamentation or set out music; if burial goods in any way transgressed rank, they were all to be compelled and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 3 (823) as well, commoners were forbidden to adorn funeral rites with gold, silver, brocade, or musical performance; any burial goods that smacked of presumption were to be seized and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 臣等參詳子孫之葬父祖，卑幼之葬尊親，全尚樸素即有傷孝道。

translations.literal: Your subjects have examined in detail that when sons and grandsons bury fathers and grandfathers, or juniors bury their elders, to insist entirely on plainness would injure filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: We find that when descendants bury parents and grandparents, or juniors bury their seniors, demanding utter austerity would itself wound filial piety.

sentences.zh: 其所用錦繡，伏請不加禁 斷。

translations.literal: As for the brocades they use, we humbly request that no prohibition be added.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore ask that brocade furnishings not be banned outright.

sentences.zh: 其用音樂及欄街設祭，身無官而葬用方相者，望嚴禁之。

translations.literal: As for the use of music and setting up sacrifices across the streets, and those without office who use the fangxiang at burial, we hope these will be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Music, street-side sacrifice displays, and the use of the exorcist figure fangxiang by persons holding no office should, we urge, be strictly prohibited.

sentences.zh: 其詔葬設祭者不在此限。

translations.literal: Those for whom the court orders burial and who set up sacrifices are not within this limit.
translations.idiomatic: Imperially mandated burials with public sacrifices are excepted.

sentences.zh: 又準後唐長興二年詔：五品、六品常參官，喪輿舁者二十人，輓歌八人，明器 三十事，共置八床；

translations.literal: Again, according to the edict of the second year of Changxing of Later Tang: for regular-attendance officials of the fifth and sixth ranks, the funeral carriage had twenty bearers, eight dirge singers, thirty pieces of grave goods, set out on eight biers in all;
translations.idiomatic: They also cited Later Tang Changxing 2 (931): fifth- and sixth-rank officials attending court daily were allotted twenty pallbearers, eight dirge singers, thirty grave figurines on eight display biers;

sentences.zh: 七品常參官舁者十六人，輓歌六人，明器二十事，置六床；

translations.literal: for seventh-rank regular-attendance officials, sixteen bearers, six dirge singers, twenty grave goods, set on six biers;
translations.idiomatic: seventh-rank officials sixteen bearers, six dirge singers, twenty figurines on six biers;

sentences.zh: 六品以下京官及檢校、試官等，舁者十二人，輓歌四人，明器十五事，置五床，並許 設紗籠二。

translations.literal: for capital officials of the sixth rank and below, and acting and probationary officials, twelve bearers, four dirge singers, fifteen grave goods on five biers, and they were all permitted two gauze canopies;
translations.idiomatic: capital officials of sixth rank and below, plus acting and probationary appointees, twelve bearers, four dirge singers, fifteen figurines on five biers, with two gauze pavilions allowed;

sentences.zh: 庶人，舁者八人，明器十二事，置兩床。

translations.literal: for commoners, eight bearers, twelve grave goods, set on two biers.
translations.idiomatic: commoners eight bearers, twelve figurines on two biers.

sentences.zh: 悉用香輿、魂車。

translations.literal: All were to use the incense carriage and soul carriage.
translations.idiomatic: All ranks were to use the incense carriage and soul carriage.

sentences.zh: 其品官葬祖父母、父母，品卑者聽以子品，葬妻子者遞降一等，其四品以上依令式施行。

translations.literal: When ranked officials buried grandparents or parents, those of lower rank were permitted to use their son's rank; when burying wife or children, each step down one grade; for the fourth rank and above, the statutes and forms were to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: When an official buried grandparents or parents, a lower-ranking mourner might adopt his son's rank; burials for wife or children dropped one grade each; fourth rank and above followed the codified forms.

sentences.zh: 望令 御史臺、街司頒行，限百日率從新製；

translations.literal: It is hoped that the Censorate and street offices will promulgate this, with a limit of one hundred days for all to follow the new regulations;
translations.idiomatic: They asked the Censorate and street patrol offices to publish the rules and give everyone a hundred days to comply;

sentences.zh: 限滿違者，以違禁之物給巡司為賞。

translations.literal: when the limit expired, violators' forbidden goods were to be given to the patrol offices as reward.
translations.idiomatic: after the deadline, confiscated contraband would reward the patrol squads.

sentences.zh: 喪家輒舉樂者，譴伶人。

translations.literal: If the bereaved household presumptuously held music, the musicians were to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Households that played music anyway were to have their musicians punished.

sentences.zh: 他不如製者，但罪下里工作。」

translations.literal: For other failures to meet the regulations, only the neighborhood craftsmen were to be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Other infractions would be charged only against the local artisans who supplied the funeral."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔 曰：「訪聞喪葬之家，有舉樂及令章者。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict stated: "We have learned that among funeral households there are those who hold music and command performances.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (984) an edict declared: "We hear that some funeral households stage music and hire entertainers.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞鄰裏之內，喪不相舂，苴麻之旁，食未嘗飽，此聖王教化之道，治世不刊之言。

translations.literal: It is said that within the neighborhood one does not pound grain during mourning, and beside the hemp of mourning one has never eaten his fill—this is the way of the sage kings' transforming instruction, words for a well-governed age that cannot be effaced.
translations.idiomatic: Custom holds that neighbors cease pounding grain for the bereaved and that mourners in hemp do not eat their fill—teachings of the sage kings, maxims no well-ordered age should forget.

sentences.zh: 何乃匪人，親罹釁酷，或則舉奠之際歌 吹為娛，靈柩之前令章為戲，甚傷風教，實紊人倫。

translations.literal: How is it that wicked persons, having themselves suffered bereavement, at the offering rite make song and pipes their amusement, or before the coffin make command performances their play—this greatly wounds custom and teaching and truly disorders human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some wretches, even while mourning their own dead, turn the offering service into song and revelry or stage entertainments before the coffin—an outrage to public morals and a breach of human decency.

sentences.zh: 今後有犯此者，並以不孝論，預坐人等第科斷。

translations.literal: Hereafter, whoever violates this shall all be judged unfilial, and those who took part shall be sentenced by graded statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth such offenders will be prosecuted as unfilial, with accomplices punished by degree.

sentences.zh: 所在官吏，常加覺察，如不用心，並當連坐。」

translations.literal: Local officials are constantly to increase surveillance; if they do not attend to it, they too shall be punished by association."
translations.idiomatic: Local officials must watch constantly; negligence will bring collective punishment."

sentences.zh: 景德二年，開封府言：「文武官亡歿，諸寺擊鍾未有定制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, the Kaifeng prefectural government reported: "When civil and military officials die, the temples' striking of bells has no fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 2 (1005) Kaifeng reported: "When officials die, temple bell-ringing lacks a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 欲望自今大卿監、大將軍、觀察使、命婦郡夫人已上，即據狀聞奏，許於天清、開寶二寺擊鍾，其聲數旋俟進止，自餘悉禁。」

translations.literal: It is desired that from now on, for grand councilors and commissioners, grand generals, observation commissioners, and titled ladies of county mistress rank and above, upon reporting according to the facts, bell-striking at the Tianqing and Kaibao temples be permitted, the number of strokes to await imperial decision; all others are forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth grand councilors, commissioners, grand generals, observation commissioners, and titled ladies of county mistress rank or higher should report deaths and be allowed bell-ringing at Tianqing and Kaibao temples, the number of strokes subject to imperial approval; all others are barred."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十七年，監登聞鼓院範同言：「今民俗有所謂火化者，生則奉養之具唯恐不至，死則燔爇而棄捐之，何獨厚於生而薄於死乎？

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing, Supervisor of the Petition Drum Court Fan Tong said: "Today among the people there is what is called cremation: while alive, the furnishings for their support are feared not to be complete enough, yet when dead they are burned and cast away—why be generous to life and stingy toward death alone?
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 27 (1157) Fan Tong of the Petition Drum Court wrote: "A custom called cremation has spread: families spare no expense while the living are cared for, yet on death they burn the body and discard the ashes—why honor life and slight the dead?

sentences.zh: 甚者焚而置之水中，識者見之 動心。

translations.literal: In extreme cases they burn the body and set it in water; those with understanding, seeing it, are moved in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Some even cast the ashes into rivers—a sight that stirs any thoughtful observer.

sentences.zh: 國朝著令，貧無葬地者，許以係官之地安葬。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has established regulations: those too poor to have burial ground are permitted to bury in government-held land.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty already allows the poor without burial plots to use state land.

sentences.zh: 河東地狹人眾，雖至親之喪，悉皆焚棄。

translations.literal: In Hedong the land is narrow and the people numerous; even for the closest kin's mourning, all are burned and discarded.
translations.idiomatic: In Hedong, where land is scarce and population dense, even the closest kin are cremated.

sentences.zh: 韓琦鎮并州，以官錢市田數頃，給民安葬，至今為美談。

translations.literal: When Han Qi governed Bingzhou, he used official funds to buy several qing of fields and gave them to the people for burial; to this day it is praised in fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi governed Bingzhou he bought fields with public funds for common burials—a deed still remembered.

sentences.zh: 然則承流宣 化，使民不畔於禮法，正守臣之職也。

translations.literal: Thus to receive the current and proclaim transformation, so that the people do not turn from ritual and law, is precisely the duty of guarding ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Guiding the people back to ritual and law is precisely a local official's duty.

sentences.zh: 方今火葬之慘，日益熾甚，事關風化，理宜禁止。

translations.literal: At present the cruelty of cremation grows daily more fierce; the matter touches custom and transformation, and by right ought to be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Cremation grows ever more common and touches public morals; it should be banned.

sentences.zh: 仍飭守臣措置荒閑之地，使貧民得以收葬，少裨風化之美。」

translations.literal: Moreover, guarding ministers should be ordered to arrange idle wasteland so that the poor may obtain burial, slightly aiding the beauty of custom and transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Local officials should also set aside wasteland so the poor can bury their dead, modestly restoring proper custom."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十八 年，戶部侍郎榮薿言：「比因臣僚陳請禁火葬，令州郡置荒閑之地，使貧民得以收葬，誠為善政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, Vice Minister of Revenue Rong Wei said: "Recently because officials memorialized to forbid cremation and ordered prefectures and districts to set aside idle wasteland so the poor might obtain burial, this is truly good government.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1158) Vice Minister of Revenue Rong Wei noted: "The recent ban on cremation and order to set aside burial ground for the poor is admirable policy.

sentences.zh: 臣聞吳越之俗，葬送費廣，必積累而後辦。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in the custom of Wu and Yue, funeral expenses are broad and one must accumulate before they can be managed.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu and Yue, I hear, funerals are so costly that families must save for years.

sentences.zh: 至於貧下之家，送終之 具，唯務從簡，是以從來率以火化為便，相習成風，勢難遽革。

translations.literal: As for poor households, the furnishings for seeing off the dead aim only at simplicity; therefore from old they have generally taken cremation as convenient, the practice becoming custom by repetition, and the momentum makes sudden reform difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Poor families keep funerals minimal and have long favored cremation as convenient—a habit hard to uproot overnight.

sentences.zh: 況州縣休息之久，生聚日繁，所用之地，必須寬廣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the prefectures and districts have rested long; population and gathering grow daily; the land used must necessarily be broad.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace populations have swelled, so burial grounds must be ample.

sentences.zh: 乃附郭近便處，官司以艱得之故，有未行摽撥 者。

translations.literal: Yet at convenient places near the outer walls, because the government offices find acquisition difficult, there are some not yet marked off and allocated.
translations.idiomatic: Near city walls, officials have not yet marked off plots because land is hard to obtain.

sentences.zh: 既葬埋未有處所，而行火化之禁，恐非人情所安。

translations.literal: Since burial places are not yet available, yet the ban on cremation is enforced, I fear this may not be what human feeling can accept.
translations.idiomatic: To forbid cremation before burial ground exists may distress the people.

sentences.zh: 欲乞除豪富士族申嚴禁止外，貧下之民並客旅遠方之人，若有死亡，姑從其便，候將來州縣摽撥到荒閑之地， 別行取旨。」

translations.literal: I wish to request that apart from strictly forbidding wealthy great clans, for poor people and travelers from afar, if there is death, for the present let them follow convenience; when later the prefectures and districts have marked off idle wasteland, separate orders may be sought."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from strict enforcement among wealthy elites, let the poor and traveling strangers cremate for now until counties allocate wasteland, then seek further instructions."

sentences.zh: 詔依，仍令諸州依已降指揮，措置摽撥。

translations.literal: An edict followed this, and the various prefectures were still ordered to arrange marking and allocation according to the directives already issued.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed but still ordered every prefecture to set aside burial ground as previously directed.

sentences.zh: 服紀。

translations.literal: Mourning garb regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress regulations.

sentences.zh: 宋天子及諸臣服制，前史皆散記諸禮中，未嘗特錄之也，後史則表而出之。

translations.literal: The mourning regulations of the Song Son of Heaven and the various subjects: earlier histories all recorded them scattered among the rites and never set them forth separately; later histories tabulate and bring them out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories scattered Song imperial and official mourning dress among general rite chapters; this history sets them out in a dedicated record.

sentences.zh: 高宗於外廷以 日易月，於內廷則行三年之禮，禦朝則淺素、淺黃。

translations.literal: Gaozong in the outer court substituted days for months, but in the inner court practiced the three-year rites; when holding court he wore pale plain and pale yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong shortened mourning to a month in public ceremony but observed three years within the palace, wearing pale white or pale yellow at court.

sentences.zh: 孝宗又力持三年之制。

translations.literal: Xiaozong again vigorously upheld the three-year regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong in turn insisted on the full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 皇帝未成服，則素紗軟腳襆頭、白羅袍、黑銀帶、絲鞋。

translations.literal: Before the emperor completed mourning dress, he wore plain gauze soft-foot wrap cap, white silk robe, black silver belt, and silk shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Before assuming full mourning, the emperor wore a plain gauze soft-foot cap, white silk robe, black silver belt, and silk shoes.

sentences.zh: 成服日，布梁冠

translations.literal: On the day of completing mourning dress, cloth beam crown
translations.idiomatic: On the day of assuming mourning dress, a cloth beam crown

sentences.zh: 〈（朱熹云：當用 十二梁）〉、

translations.literal: (Zhu Xi said: one should use twelve beams),
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi noted: it should have twelve beams),

sentences.zh: 首絰、直領布大袖衫

translations.literal: head mourning band, straight-collared cloth large-sleeved shirt
translations.idiomatic: head mourning band, straight-collared cloth large-sleeved shirt

sentences.zh: 〈（朱熹云：不當用襽，蓋下已有裙）〉、

translations.literal: (Zhu Xi said: one should not use the cross-collar over-garment, for below there is already a skirt),
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi said: the cross-collar over-garment should not be used, since a skirt is worn below),

sentences.zh: 布裙、褲、腰絰、竹杖、白綾襯衫，或斜巾、帽子。

translations.literal: cloth skirt, trousers, waist mourning band, bamboo staff, white damask undershirt, or slanting kerchief and cap.
translations.idiomatic: cloth skirt, trousers, waist mourning band, bamboo staff, white damask undershirt, or alternatively a slanting kerchief and cap.

sentences.zh: 視事日，去杖、首絰。

translations.literal: On the day of attending to affairs, he removed staff and head mourning band.
translations.idiomatic: When resuming governance he set aside staff and head band.

sentences.zh: 小祥日，改服布 襆頭、襽衫、腰絰、布褲。

translations.literal: On the day of lesser felicitations, he changed to cloth wrap cap, cross-collar mourning shirt, waist mourning band, and cloth trousers.
translations.idiomatic: At lesser felicitations he changed to a cloth wrap cap, cross-collar mourning shirt, waist band, and cloth trousers.

sentences.zh: 大祥畢，服素紗軟腳襆頭、白羅袍、素履、黑銀帶。

translations.literal: When greater felicitations were completed, he wore plain gauze soft-foot wrap cap, white silk robe, plain shoes, and black silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: After greater felicitations he wore plain gauze soft-foot cap, white silk robe, plain shoes, and black silver belt.

sentences.zh: 禫祭畢，素紗軟腳襆頭、淺色黃羅袍、黑銀帶。

translations.literal: When the chan sacrifice was completed, plain gauze soft-foot wrap cap, light-colored yellow silk robe, black silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: After the chan sacrifice, plain gauze soft-foot cap, pale yellow silk robe, and black silver belt.

sentences.zh: 祔廟日，服履、黃袍、紅帶。

translations.literal: On the day of enshrining in the ancestral temple, he wore shoes, yellow robe, and red belt.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of enshrinement in the ancestral temple he wore shoes, a yellow robe, and a red belt.

sentences.zh: 禦正 殿視事，則皂襆頭、淡黃袍、黑鞓犀帶、素絲鞋。

translations.literal: When holding court in the main hall, then black wrap cap, pale yellow robe, black rhinoceros-hide belt, and plain silk shoes.
translations.idiomatic: When holding court in the main hall he wore a black wrap cap, pale yellow robe, black rhinoceros-hide belt, and plain silk shoes.

sentences.zh: 此中興後製也。

translations.literal: This is the regulation after the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: These were the regulations after the Southern restoration.

sentences.zh: 孝宗居憂，再定三年之制。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was in mourning, he again fixed the three-year regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning, Xiaozong reinstated the three-year rule.

sentences.zh: 其服：布冠、直領大袖衫、布裙、首絰、腰絰、竹杖。

translations.literal: His dress: cloth crown, straight-collared large-sleeved shirt, cloth skirt, head mourning band, waist mourning band, bamboo staff.
translations.idiomatic: His mourning dress comprised a cloth crown, straight-collared large-sleeved shirt, cloth skirt, head and waist bands, and bamboo staff.

sentences.zh: 小 祥不易服。

translations.literal: At lesser felicitations he did not change dress.
translations.idiomatic: At lesser felicitations he did not change garments.

sentences.zh: 大祥禮畢，始去杖、去絰。

translations.literal: When the rites of greater felicitations were completed, only then did he remove staff and mourning bands.
translations.idiomatic: Only after greater felicitations did he lay aside staff and bands.

sentences.zh: 禫祭畢，始服素紗軟腳襆頭、白袍、黑銀帶。

translations.literal: When the chan sacrifice was completed, he first wore plain gauze soft-foot wrap cap, white robe, and black silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: After the chan sacrifice he first wore plain gauze soft-foot cap, white robe, and black silver belt.

sentences.zh: 祔廟畢，服皂襆頭、黑鞓犀帶。

translations.literal: When enshrinement in the temple was completed, he wore black wrap cap and black rhinoceros-hide belt.
translations.idiomatic: After enshrinement he wore a black wrap cap and black rhinoceros-hide belt.

sentences.zh: 每遇過宮廟謁，則衰絰行禮，二十五月而除。

translations.literal: Whenever he passed the palace temples to pay respects, he performed the rites in the coarsest mourning bands, and after twenty-five months removed them.
translations.idiomatic: On visits to the ancestral shrines he wore the coarsest mourning bands until the twenty-fifth month.

sentences.zh: 三 年之內，禁中常服布巾、布衫、布背子。

translations.literal: Within the three years, in the forbidden precinct he regularly wore cloth kerchief, cloth shirt, and cloth jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the three years within the palace he routinely wore cloth kerchief, shirt, and jacket.

sentences.zh: 視事則禦內殿，服白布襆頭、白布袍、黑銀帶，殿設素幄。

translations.literal: When attending to affairs he held court in the inner hall, wearing white cloth wrap cap, white cloth robe, and black silver belt; the hall was set with plain curtains.
translations.idiomatic: When governing he held court in the inner hall in white cloth cap and robe with black silver belt, the hall draped in plain curtains.

sentences.zh: 每五日一次過宮，則衰絰而杖。

translations.literal: Every five days, once when passing the palace, he wore the coarsest mourning bands and carried the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Every five days on a palace visit he wore coarsest mourning bands and carried the staff.

sentences.zh: 虞祭則布折上巾、黑帶、布袍。

translations.literal: At the yu sacrifice he wore cloth folded-up kerchief, black belt, and cloth robe.
translations.idiomatic: At the yu sacrifice he wore a cloth folded kerchief, black belt, and cloth robe.

sentences.zh: 受金使吊則衰絰，禦德壽殿東廊之素幄。

translations.literal: When receiving the Jin envoy for mourning condolences, he wore the coarsest mourning bands and held court in the plain curtains of the eastern corridor of the Deshou Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving the Jin mourning envoy he wore coarsest mourning bands and held audience in plain curtains in the eastern corridor of Deshou Hall.

sentences.zh: 受賀節使，則禦垂拱殿東楹之素幄。

translations.literal: When receiving the congratulatory festival envoy, he held court in the plain curtains of the eastern pillar of the Chui'gong Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When receiving congratulatory festival envoys he held audience in plain curtains at the eastern bay of Chui'gong Hall.

sentences.zh: 是時，宰執、近臣皆不肯行，惟斷自上心，堅不可奪，大臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: At that time the chief ministers and close attendants all refused to practice it; only the decision came from the emperor's own heart, firm and not to be wrested away, and the great ministers then did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers and close attendants all refused to follow suit, but the emperor's resolve was unshakable and they dared not object.

sentences.zh: 讚其決者，惟敕 局下僚沈清臣一人而已。

translations.literal: The one who praised his resolution was only Shen Qingchen, a subordinate clerk of the Edict Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shen Qingchen, a junior clerk of the Edict Bureau, praised his resolve.

sentences.zh: 臣為君服，宋制有三等：中書門下、樞密使副、尚書、翰林學士、節度使、金吾上將軍、文武二品以上，布梁冠、直領大袖 衫、布裙、褲、腰絰、竹杖，或布襆頭、襴衫、布斜巾、絹襯服。

translations.literal: When subjects mourned for the ruler, Song regulations had three grades: for the Secretariat-Chancellery, vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, ministers, Hanlin academicians, military commissioners, commanders-in-chief of the Golden Crow Guards, and civil and military officials of the second rank and above—cloth beam crown, straight-collared large-sleeved shirt, cloth skirt, trousers, waist mourning band, bamboo staff, or cloth wrap cap, brocade mourning shirt, cloth slanting kerchief, and silk undershirt.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress for the emperor fell into three Song grades: Secretariat-Chancellery, Bureau of Military Affairs deputies, ministers, Hanlin academicians, commissioners, Golden Crow commanders, and officials of second rank and above wore cloth beam crown, straight-collared large-sleeved shirt, skirt, trousers, waist band, and staff—or alternatively cloth cap, brocade mourning shirt, slanting kerchief, and silk undershirt.

sentences.zh: 文武五品以上並職事官監察御史以上、內客省、宣政、昭宣、知閣門事、前殿都知、押班，布梁 冠、直領大袖衫、裙、褲、腰絰，或襆頭、襽衫。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above, and functional officials including surveillance censors and above, Inner Service Bureau, Xuanzheng, Zhaoxuan, gate commissioners, front-hall directors, and duty officers—cloth beam crown, straight-collared large-sleeved shirt, skirt, trousers, waist mourning band, or wrap cap and cross-collar mourning shirt.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above, surveillance censors and above, Inner Service and palace gate officials wore cloth beam crown, straight-collared large-sleeved shirt, skirt, trousers, and waist band—or wrap cap and cross-collar mourning shirt.

sentences.zh: 自餘文武百官，布襆頭、襽衫、腰絰而已。

translations.literal: All remaining civil and military officials wore only cloth wrap cap, cross-collar mourning shirt, and waist mourning band.
translations.idiomatic: All other officials wore only cloth cap, cross-collar mourning shirt, and waist band.

sentences.zh: 入局治事，並不易服。

translations.literal: When entering their bureaus to handle affairs, none changed dress.
translations.idiomatic: They did not change dress when entering office to conduct business.

sentences.zh: 宰執奏事去杖，小祥去冠，餘官奏事如之。

translations.literal: Chief ministers reporting affairs removed the staff; at lesser felicitations they removed the crown; other officials reporting affairs did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers set aside the staff when reporting and the crown at lesser felicitations; other officials followed suit.

sentences.zh: 大祥，素紗軟腳折上巾、黲公服、白鞓錫帶。

translations.literal: At greater felicitations, plain gauze soft-foot folded-up kerchief, gray official robe, white tin belt.
translations.idiomatic: At greater felicitations they wore plain gauze soft-foot folded kerchief, gray official robe, and white tin belt.

sentences.zh: 禫除畢，去黲服，常服仍黑帶、皂鞍韉。

translations.literal: When chan removal was completed, they removed the gray robe; regular dress still had black belt and black saddle trappings.
translations.idiomatic: After chan removal they shed the gray robe but still wore black belt and black saddle trappings in regular dress.

sentences.zh: 祔廟畢，始純吉服。

translations.literal: When enshrinement in the temple was completed, they first wore purely auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: Only after enshrinement did they wear fully auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 宗室出則常服，居則衰麻以終製。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen going out wore regular dress; dwelling within, they wore coarse hemp to the end of the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen wore regular dress in public but coarse hemp at home until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 光宗居孝 宗之憂，趙汝愚當國，始令群臣服白涼衫、皂帶治事，逮終製乃止。

translations.literal: When Guangzong was in mourning for Xiaozong, Zhao Ruyu held the state, and first ordered the various ministers to wear white cool shirts and black belts when handling affairs, continuing until the regulation ended.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong mourned Xiaozong, Zhao Ruyu governing ordered officials to conduct business in white cool shirts and black belts until mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 寧宗居光宗之憂，復令百官以日易月，禫除畢，服紫衫、皂帶以治事，從禮部侍郎陳宗召請也。

translations.literal: When Ningzong was in mourning for Guangzong, he again ordered the hundred officials to substitute days for months; when chan removal was completed, they wore purple shirts and black belts to handle affairs, following the request of Vice Minister of Rites Chen Zongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong mourned Guangzong he again shortened mourning to a month; after chan removal officials governed in purple shirts and black belts at Vice Minister of Rites Chen Zongzhao's request.

sentences.zh: 諸路監司、州軍縣鎮長吏以下，服布四腳、直領布襽衫、麻腰絰，朝晡臨，三日除之。

translations.literal: Supervisors of the circuits, prefectural, district, and county chief officials and below wore cloth four-corner kerchief, straight-collared cloth cross-collar mourning shirt, and hemp waist mourning band; they attended morning and evening audiences for three days and then removed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit supervisors and local magistrates wore cloth four-corner kerchief, straight-collared cross-collar mourning shirt, and hemp waist band, attending morning and evening for three days only.

sentences.zh: 內外命婦當入臨者，布裙、衫、帔、首絰、絹襯衫帕首。

translations.literal: Titled ladies inside and outside the court who were to enter for condolence wore cloth skirt, shirt, stole, head mourning band, silk undershirt, and kerchief headwrap.
translations.idiomatic: Titled ladies attending condolence wore cloth skirt, shirt, stole, head band, silk undershirt, and kerchief headwrap.

sentences.zh: 士庶於本家素服， 三日而除。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners at their own homes wore plain dress for three days and then removed it.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners wore plain dress at home for three days.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁，服除外不禁。

translations.literal: Marriage and betrothal were not forbidden except for mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage was permitted except during the mourning period itself.

sentences.zh: 文武臣僚之家，至山陵祔畢，乃許嫁娶，仍不用花彩及樂。

translations.literal: Households of civil and military officials were permitted marriage only when the mountain tomb enshrinement was completed, and still might not use floral ornament or music.
translations.idiomatic: Official households might marry only after the imperial tomb enshrinement, and still without floral display or music.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年十月，以將作監韋璞充金國告哀使，閣門舍人薑 特立副之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourteenth year of Chunxi, Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings Wei Pu was appointed Jin-state mourning envoy, with Gate Attendant Jiang Teli as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Chunxi 14 (1187) Wei Pu of the Palace Buildings Directorate was sent as mourning envoy to Jin, with Gate Attendant Jiang Teli as deputy.

sentences.zh: 禮部、太堂寺言：「告哀使、副並三節人，從禮例，如在大祥內，合服布襆頭、礻闌衫、布褲、腰絰，布涼傘，鞍韉；

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites and the Directorate of Sacrifices reported: "The mourning envoy, deputy, and three-rank envoys alike, following ritual precedent—as if within the da-xiang period—should wear cloth futou, cross-collar mourning shirt, cloth trousers, waist mourning band, cloth cool parasol, and saddle blanket;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and Directorate of Sacrifices reported: "The mourning envoy, his deputy, and the three-rank escorts should follow precedent: during the da-xiang mourning period they were to wear cloth futou, cross-collar mourning shirt, cloth trousers, waist band, cloth parasol, and saddle trappings;

sentences.zh: 在禫服內，合服素紗軟腳襆頭、黲 色公服、黑鞓犀帶，青傘，皂鞍韉；

translations.literal: Within the chan mourning period, they should wear plain gauze soft-foot futou, dun-colored official uniform, black belt with rhinoceros-horn buckle, green parasol, and black saddle blanket;
translations.idiomatic: During chan mourning they should wear plain gauze soft-foot futou, dun official dress, black rhinoceros-horn belt, green parasol, and black saddle trappings;

sentences.zh: 俟禫除，即從吉服，仍係黑帶，去魚，涼傘、韉並從禫制，並去狨座。

translations.literal: Awaiting chan removal, they then followed auspicious dress, still tied with black belt, removed the fish badge, cool parasol and blanket both following chan regulations, and also removed the leopard-skin seat.
translations.idiomatic: After chan removal they reverted to regular dress but kept the black belt, removed the fish badge, retained chan-style parasol and saddle trappings, and gave up the leopard-skin saddle pad.

sentences.zh: 三節人衣紫衫、黑帶，並不聽樂，不射弓弩，候過界， 聽使、副審度，隨宜改易服用。」

translations.literal: The three-rank envoys wore purple shirts and black belts, and altogether were forbidden music and forbidden shooting bow and crossbow; awaiting crossing the border, the envoy and deputy were permitted to assess and change dress as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: The three-rank escorts wore purple shirts and black belts, abstained from music and archery, and after crossing the border the envoy and deputy might adjust dress as they saw fit."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 或遣留遺信物使，同上服。

translations.literal: Sometimes envoys were dispatched to leave behind testamentary tokens; they wore the same dress as above.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys sent to deliver testamentary tokens followed the same dress code.

sentences.zh: 喪服雜議。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous discussions on mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous Mourning-Dress Debates

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，侍御史吳鼎臣言：「武班及諸職司人吏，曾因親喪出入禁 門，甚有裹素紗襆頭者，殊失肅下尊上之禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli, Attending Censor Wu Dingchen said: "Military ranks and various office clerks, having once passed through the forbidden gates during kin mourning, many wrapped plain gauze futou—greatly failing the ritual of subordinates respecting superiors.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 7 (1047) Attending Censor Wu Dingchen said: "Military officials and clerks entering the palace gates in mourning sometimes wore plain gauze futou, gravely violating court decorum.

sentences.zh: 欲乞武兩班，除以官品起復許裹素紗外，其餘臣僚並諸職司人吏，雖有親喪服未除，並須光紗加首，不得更裹素紗。」

translations.literal: I wish to request that for the two military ranks, apart from those permitted plain gauze when recalled to office by rank, all other officials and office clerks, though kin mourning dress is not yet removed, must all use glossy gauze on the head and may not again wrap plain gauze."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that apart from military officers recalled by rank, all others in mourning wear glossy gauze headwraps rather than plain gauze, even before mourning ended."

sentences.zh: 詔送太常禮院。

translations.literal: An edict sent it to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「準令文，凶服不入公門。

translations.literal: Ritual officials said: "According to statute, mourning dress does not enter the public gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials replied: "Statute forbade mourning dress in government halls.

sentences.zh: 其遭喪被起，在朝參處，常服各依品服，惟色以淺，無金玉飾；

translations.literal: Those stricken by mourning but recalled to service, at court audience places, wore regular dress each according to rank dress, only the color lighter, without gold and jade ornament;
translations.idiomatic: Officials recalled from mourning wore rank-appropriate regular dress at court, in lighter colors and without gold or jade ornaments;

sentences.zh: 在家，依其服制。

translations.literal: At home, they followed their mourning regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At home they observed full mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 其被起者，及期喪以下居式假 者，衣冠朝集，皆聽不預。

translations.literal: Those recalled, and those dwelling in ritual leave for lesser mourning and below—all at cap-and-gown court assemblies were permitted not to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled officials and those on ritual leave for lesser mourning were excused from formal court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 今鼎臣所奏，有礙令文。」

translations.literal: Now Dingchen's memorial conflicts with the statute."
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen's proposal, they said, conflicted with existing law."

sentences.zh: 詔依所定，如遇筵宴，其服淺色素紗人，更不令祗應。

translations.literal: An edict followed the established rule; when encountering banquets, those in light-colored plain gauze were no longer ordered to attend.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this ruling and barred officials in light plain gauze from serving at banquets.

sentences.zh: 丁父母憂。

translations.literal: Mourning for father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: Parental Mourning

sentences.zh: 淳化五年八月，詔曰：「孝為 百行之本，喪有三年之制，著於典禮，以厚人倫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Chunhua, an edict said: "Filial piety is the root of the hundred conduct; mourning has the three-year regulation, recorded in canonical ritual, to enrich human relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chunhua 5 (994) an edict declared: "Filial piety is the foundation of virtue and the three-year mourning rule part of canonical ritual to strengthen human bonds.

sentences.zh: 中外文武官子弟，或父兄之淪亡，蒙朝廷之齒敘，未及卒哭，已聞蒞官，遽忘哀戚，頗玷風教。

translations.literal: Sons and younger brothers of civil and military officials inside and outside, when fathers or elder brothers passed away, received the court's rank ordering—before reaching the end of wailing they already heard of taking office, hastily forgetting grief, greatly staining customary teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Younger relatives of officials appointed by the court often took office before mourning wailing ended, forgetting grief and disgracing public morals.

sentences.zh: 自今文武官子弟， 有因父亡兄歿特被敘用，未經百日，不得趣赴公參。

translations.literal: From now on sons of civil and military officials who, because father died or elder brother passed, were specially ordered into service—without passing a hundred days, may not hasten to attend public audience.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth officials' sons appointed after a father's or brother's death might not attend court before a hundred days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 御史臺專加糾察；

translations.literal: The Censorate was specially charged to investigate;
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate would enforce this;

sentences.zh: 並有冒哀求仕、釋服從吉者，並以名聞。」

translations.literal: and any who falsely claimed mourning to seek office or removed mourning dress to follow auspicious rites—all were to be reported by name."
translations.idiomatic: and anyone who feigned mourning for appointment or ended mourning prematurely was to be reported by name."

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，詔任三司、館閣職事者丁憂，並令持服。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, an edict: those holding Three Departments and Pavilion posts who entered mourning were all ordered to observe mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 1 (998) officials in Three Departments and Pavilion posts were required to observe full mourning.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「川峽、廣南、福建路官，丁憂不得離任，既受代而喪製未畢者，許其終製。」

translations.literal: Again an edict: "Officials of the Sichuan gorges, Guangnan, and Fujian circuits—entering mourning could not leave post; those who had already been replaced while mourning regulation was not yet completed were permitted to finish the regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict barred officials in remote circuits from leaving post during mourning, but allowed replaced officials to complete mourning at post."

sentences.zh: 尋令川峽官，除州軍長吏奏裁，餘並許解官。

translations.literal: Soon it was ordered for Sichuan gorge officials: except for prefectural and district chief officials who required memorial and decision, the rest were all permitted to resign office.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the gorges circuits were soon allowed to resign, except prefectural chiefs who needed imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，殿中侍御史張廓言：「京朝官丁父母憂者，多因陳乞，與免持服。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Palace Censor Zhang Kuo said: "Capital officials mourning for parents often, through petition, were granted exemption from observing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 9 (1016) Palace Censor Zhang Kuo said: "Capital officials mourning parents often petitioned to skip mourning altogether.

sentences.zh: 且忠教恩義，士所執守，一悖於禮，其何能立？

translations.literal: Moreover loyalty, teaching, grace, and righteousness are what scholars uphold—once one violates ritual, how can one stand?
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and righteousness define the scholar; violate ritual once and what moral standing remains?

sentences.zh: 今執事盈庭，各務簡易，況無金革之事，中外之官不闕，不可習以為例。

translations.literal: Now officeholders fill the court, each pursuing ease; moreover there are no war-and-armor affairs, officials inside and outside are not lacking—this must not become habitual precedent.
translations.idiomatic: With a full court and no military emergency, he argued, easing mourning must not become custom.

sentences.zh: 望自後並依典禮，三年服滿，得赴朝請。」

translations.literal: I hope from now on all follow canonical ritual, three-year mourning completed, then permitted to attend court audience."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that hereafter all observe canonical three-year mourning before returning to court."

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，御史臺言：「文武官並丁憂者，相承服五十四月，別無條例。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, the Censorate said: "Civil and military officials alike entering mourning successively observe fifty-four months, with no separate regulation."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 4 (1020) the Censorate reported: "Officials in parental mourning customarily served fifty-four months without statutory basis."

sentences.zh: 下太常，禮官議曰：「按《禮·喪服小記》云：『父母之喪偕，先葬者不虞、祔，待後 事，其葬服斬衰。』

translations.literal: It was sent down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; ritual officials deliberated: "According to the Records of Rites, Mourning Dress Minor Note says: 'When parents' mourning coincides, the one buried first does not receive yu or fu rites; awaiting later matters, burial dress is zhan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: Referred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, ritual officials cited the Records of Rites: when both parents die together, the first buried skips certain rites and wears the heaviest mourning at burial.

sentences.zh: 《注》：『謂同月若同日死也。

translations.literal: Commentary: 'Meaning dying in the same month or same day.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains this means death in the same month or day.

sentences.zh: 先葬者母也，其葬服斬衰者，喪之隆哀宜從重也。

translations.literal: The one buried first is the mother; that burial dress is zhan-sui—mourning's utmost grief should follow the heavier.
translations.idiomatic: When the mother is buried first, the heavier zhan-sui at burial reflects the principle of mourning at its fullest.

sentences.zh: 假令父死在前月而同月葬，猶服斬衰，不葬不變服也。

translations.literal: Suppose the father died in the prior month but burial is in the same month—still wear zhan-sui; without burial one does not change dress.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the father died the month before but both are buried the same month, the heavier mourning still applies until burial.

sentences.zh: 言其葬 服斬衰，則虞、祔各以其服矣。

translations.literal: Speaking of burial dress as zhan-sui, then yu and fu each follow their respective dress.
translations.idiomatic: Once burial dress is zhan-sui, the yu and fu rites each follow their proper mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 及練、祥皆然。

translations.literal: Reaching lian and xiang, all are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle applies through lian and xiang mourning stages.

sentences.zh: 卒事，反服重。』

translations.literal: When the rite is completed, return to the heavier dress.'
translations.idiomatic: After each rite one reverts to the heavier mourning.'

sentences.zh: 《雜記》云：『有父之喪，如未沒喪而母死，其除父之喪也，服其除服，卒事，反喪服。』

translations.literal: Miscellaneous Records says: 'Having a father's mourning, if before the father's mourning is finished the mother dies, when removing the father's mourning one wears the removal dress; when the rite is completed, return to mourning dress.'
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records states that if the mother dies before the father's mourning ends, one wears the father's removal dress for that rite, then resumes mourning for the mother.'

sentences.zh: 《注》 云：『沒，猶終也。

translations.literal: Commentary says: 'Mo means finished.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary glosses mo as 'finished.'

sentences.zh: 除服謂祥祭之服，卒事既祭，反喪服，服後死者之服。』

translations.literal: Removal dress means xiang-sacrifice dress; when the rite is completed and sacrifice performed, return to mourning dress, wearing the later-deceased's dress.'
translations.idiomatic: Removal dress is the xiang-sacrifice garb; after that rite one resumes mourning for the later deceased.'

sentences.zh: 又杜預云：『若父母同日卒，其葬先母後父，皆服斬衰，其虞、祔先父後母，各服其 服，卒事，反服父服。

translations.literal: Again Du Yu said: 'If father and mother die the same day, burial is mother first then father—both wear zhan-sui; yu and fu are father first then mother, each wearing respective dress; when completed, return to father's dress.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu held that when both parents die the same day, burial is mother first but yu and fu rites honor the father first, each in proper mourning, then one resumes the father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 若父已葬而母卒，則服母之服，虞訖，反服父之服。

translations.literal: If the father is already buried and the mother dies, then wear the mother's dress; when yu is finished, return to the father's dress.
translations.idiomatic: If the father is already buried when the mother dies, one wears mourning for the mother, then after the yu rite resumes the father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 既除練，則服母之服。

translations.literal: Once lian removal is reached, then wear the mother's dress.
translations.idiomatic: At the lian removal stage one wears mourning for the mother.

sentences.zh: 喪可除，則服父之服以除之，訖則服母之服。』

translations.literal: When mourning may be removed, wear the father's dress to remove it; when finished, wear the mother's dress.'
translations.idiomatic: When the father's mourning can be ended, one wears his mourning for that removal, then resumes the mother's.'

sentences.zh: 賀循云：『父之喪 未終，又遭母喪，當父服應終之月，皆服祥祭之服，如除喪之禮。

translations.literal: He Xun said: 'The father's mourning not yet finished, again encountering the mother's mourning—in the month when the father's mourning should end, all wear xiang-sacrifice dress, as in mourning-removal ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun held that if the mother dies before the father's mourning ends, at the month the father's mourning would end one performs xiang removal as for a completed mourning.

sentences.zh: 卒事，反母之服。』

translations.literal: When the rite is completed, return to the mother's dress.'
translations.idiomatic: After that rite one resumes mourning for the mother.'

sentences.zh: 臣等參考典故，則是隨其先後而除之，無通服五十四月之文。

translations.literal: We your subjects consulted classical precedents; thus mourning is ended according to sequence—there is no text of universally wearing fifty-four months.
translations.idiomatic: They concluded that mourning ends in sequence of deaths, with no authority for a flat fifty-four-month rule.

sentences.zh: 請依舊禮改正。」

translations.literal: We request correction according to the old ritual."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that practice be corrected to follow ancient ritual."

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，太常禮院議：《禮記》：『父母之喪，無貴賤，一也。』

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual deliberated: The Book of Rites: 'Mourning for parents—without distinction of noble and base, it is one.'
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 3 (1043) the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual cited the Book of Rites: parental mourning makes no distinction of rank.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『三年之喪，人道之至大也。』

translations.literal: It also says: 'The three-year mourning is the utmost greatness of human conduct.'
translations.idiomatic: It also declares the three-year mourning the highest expression of human duty.'

sentences.zh: 請不以文武品秩高下，並聽終喪。」

translations.literal: We request that without regard to civil or military rank high or low, all be permitted to complete mourning."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that officials of every rank be allowed to complete full mourning.

sentences.zh: 時以武臣入流者雜，難盡解官。

translations.literal: At the time because military officers entering the civil stream were mixed, it was difficult to have all resign office.
translations.idiomatic: Because many military officers had entered the civil service, requiring all to resign was impractical.

sentences.zh: 詔：「自今三司副使已上，非領邊寄，並聽終製，仍續月奉。

translations.literal: An edict: "From now on Vice Commissioners of the Three Departments and above, if not holding frontier commissions, are all permitted to complete the regulation, still continuing monthly salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted: "From now on Vice Commissioners and above not on frontier duty may complete mourning while retaining salary.

sentences.zh: 武臣非在邊而願解官者聽。」

translations.literal: Military officers not on the frontier who wish to resign office are permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Military officers not on frontier duty who wished to resign to mourn were also allowed."

sentences.zh: 凡奪情之制，文臣諫舍以上，牧伯刺史以上，皆卒哭後恩製起復；

translations.literal: As for the regulation on seizing sentiment: civil remonstrance officials and above, prefects and regional inspectors and above—all after end of wailing receive grace-order recall to service;
translations.idiomatic: Under the rule of seized mourning, remonstrance officials and prefects were recalled after the wailing period;

sentences.zh: 其在切要者，不候卒哭。

translations.literal: Those in urgent posts need not await end of wailing.
translations.idiomatic: those in urgent posts could be recalled even before wailing ended.

sentences.zh: 內職遭喪，但給假而已，願終喪者亦聽。

translations.literal: Inner-court posts encountering mourning were only granted leave; those wishing to complete mourning were also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-court officials received leave for mourning, though full mourning was permitted if desired.

sentences.zh: 惟京朝、幕職、州縣官皆解官行服，亦有特追出者。

translations.literal: Only capital officials, staff appointees, and prefectural and district officials all resigned office to observe mourning; there were also those specially summoned out.
translations.idiomatic: Capital, staff, and local officials had to resign to mourn, though some were specially recalled.

sentences.zh: 凡公除與祭。

translations.literal: On public removal and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Public Removal and Sacrificial Attendance

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，禮儀使言：天聖五年，太常禮院言：自來宗廟祠祭，皆宰臣、參知政事行事，每有服制，旋復改差，多致妨闕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, the Commissioner of Ritual said: In the fifth year of Tiansheng, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual said: From old, ancestral temple sacrifices were all performed by chief ministers and Vice Directors of the Secretariat; whenever there was mourning dress, replacements were immediately reassigned, often causing obstruction and deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 2 (1035) the Commissioner of Ritual noted that since Tiansheng 5 (1027) ancestral sacrifices led by chief ministers were repeatedly disrupted when replacements had to be found for officials in mourning.

sentences.zh: 檢會《唐會要》，貞元六 年詔，百官有私喪公除者，聽赴宗廟之祭。

translations.literal: Examining the Tang Institutional Essentials, the sixth year of Zhenyuan edict: officials with private mourning public removal were permitted to attend ancestral temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They cited the Tang Institutional Essentials: a Zhenyuan 6 (790) edict allowed officials in public mourning removal to attend ancestral temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 監祭御史以《禮》有「緦麻已上喪不得饗廟」，移牒吏部詰之。

translations.literal: The supervising sacrifice censor, citing that the Rites have "mourning of si-ma and above may not partake of temple feast," sent a document to the Ministry of Personnel to interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising sacrifice censor challenged this, citing the rule that "officials in si-ma mourning or above may not attend temple feasts."

sentences.zh: 吏部奏：準《禮》，「諸侯絕周、大夫絕緦」者，所以殺 旁親，不敢廢大宗之祭事，則緦不祭者，謂同宮未葬，欲人吉凶不相黷也。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized: According to the Rites, "feudal lords cut off zhou, grandees cut off si"—thereby reducing collateral kin, not daring to abandon the great lineage's sacrificial affairs; thus si not sacrificing means co-residing and not yet buried, wishing that auspicious and inauspicious not mutually defile.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel replied that ritual limits mourning for collateral kin so as not to abandon major lineage sacrifices; the ban on si-mourning at temple applies only when a co-resident relative is unburied, to keep mourning and ritual apart—citing "feudal lords cut off zhou, grandees cut off si."

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已降，變而從權，緦已上喪服，假滿即吉，謂之公除。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, changing to follow expedient, si and above mourning dress—when leave was full then auspicious, called public removal.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward custom shifted: after leave for si-mourning or above one resumed regular dress, called public removal.

sentences.zh: 凡既葬公除，則無事不可， 故於祭無妨。

translations.literal: Generally once buried and public removal, then nothing is forbidden; thus for sacrifice there is no obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Once burial and public removal were complete, no activity was barred—including sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 乞今凡有慘服既葬公除，及聞哀假滿，許吉服赴祭。

translations.literal: We beg that now all who have coarse mourning dress buried and public removal, and those whose mourning-leave hearing is full, be permitted auspicious dress to attend sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that officials who had completed burial and public removal, or finished mourning leave, be allowed to attend sacrifices in regular dress.

sentences.zh: 同宮未葬，雖公除依前禁之。

translations.literal: Co-residing and not yet buried—even with public removal, as before forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Co-residents of an unburied relative remained barred even after public removal.

sentences.zh: 詔從。

translations.literal: An edict followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又王涇《郊祀錄》：「緦麻已上喪，不行宗廟之祭者，以明吉 凶不相干也。

translations.literal: Again Wang Jing's Record of Suburban Sacrifice: "Si-ma and above mourning, not performing ancestral temple sacrifice—is to clarify that auspicious and inauspicious do not interfere.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing's Record of Suburban Sacrifice also held: "Si-ma mourning or above barred ancestral sacrifice to keep mourning and ritual separate.

sentences.zh: 貞元，吏部奏請，得許權改吉服，以從宗廟之祭，此一時之事，非舊典也。」

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan, the Ministry of Personnel memorialized requesting permission to temporarily change to auspicious dress to follow ancestral temple sacrifice—this was a matter of one time, not the old canon."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenyuan Personnel memorial allowing temporary regular dress for temple sacrifice was an expedient of its day, not ancient precedent."

sentences.zh: 今本院看詳，律稱：「如有緦麻已上喪遣充掌事者，笞五十。」

translations.literal: Now this court has examined in detail; the code states: "If one in si-ma and above mourning is dispatched to serve as presiding officer, bamboo fifty."
translations.idiomatic: The court noted that Tang law punished assigning officials in si-ma mourning or above to preside at rites with fifty blows of the bamboo, citing the rule that "if one in si-ma mourning or above is dispatched to serve as presiding officer, bamboo fifty."

sentences.zh: 此唐初所 定。

translations.literal: This was established at the beginning of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: That rule dated from early Tang.

sentences.zh: 吏部起請，皆援引典故。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel's initiating request all cited classical precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel's petition had cited classical precedents throughout.

sentences.zh: 奉詔，百官有私喪公除者，聽赴宗廟之祭。

translations.literal: Following the edict, officials with private mourning public removal were permitted to attend ancestral temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had permitted officials in public mourning removal to attend ancestral temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後雖王涇著《郊祀錄》稱是一時之事，非舊典也。

translations.literal: Later although Wang Jing wrote in the Record of Suburban Sacrifice calling it a matter of one time, not the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Jing's Record of Suburban Sacrifice dismissed this as a temporary measure, not ancient canon.

sentences.zh: 又別無詔敕改更，是以歷代止依貞元詔命 施行。

translations.literal: Again there was no separate edict or order changing it; thus through generations only the Zhenyuan edict command was followed in practice.
translations.idiomatic: No later edict overturned it, so generations had followed the Zhenyuan order.

sentences.zh: 至大中祥符中，詳定官請依《郊祀錄》，緦麻以上喪，不預宗廟之祭。

translations.literal: Reaching Dazhong Xiangfu, examining officials requested following the Record of Suburban Sacrifice—si-ma and above mourning did not participate in ancestral temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu examining officials had sought to follow Wang Jing and bar si-ma mourning or above from ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今詳貞元起請，證據分明，王涇所說，別無典故。

translations.literal: Now examining the Zhenyuan initiating request, the evidence is clear; what Wang Jing said has no separate classical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenyuan petition rested on clear evidence; Wang Jing's view lacked supporting precedent.

sentences.zh: 望自今後有私喪公除者，聽赴宗廟之 祭，免致廢闕。

translations.literal: We hope from now on those with private mourning public removal be permitted to attend ancestral temple sacrifice, avoiding causing abandonment and deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that officials in public mourning removal again be allowed at ancestral sacrifices to prevent ritual disruption.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，禮官邵必言：「古之臣子，未有居父母喪而輒與國家大祭者。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli, ritual official Shao Bi said: "Ancient ministers and sons—none while dwelling in parents' mourning hastily joined the state's great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 7 (1047) ritual official Shao Bi said: "No ancient minister had ever joined state grand sacrifices while mourning parents.

sentences.zh: 今但不許入宗廟，至於南郊壇、景靈宮，皆許行事。

translations.literal: Now they are only forbidden entering the ancestral temple; as for the Southern Suburban altar and Jingling Palace, all are permitted to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Today they are barred from the ancestral temple yet allowed to officiate at the Southern Suburban altar and Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 按唐吏部 所請慘服既葬公除者，謂周以下也，前後相承，誤以為三年之喪，得吉服從祭，失之甚也。

translations.literal: According to what the Tang Ministry of Personnel requested—coarse mourning dress buried and public removal refers to zhou and below; successively handed down front and back, mistakenly taken as three-year mourning permitting auspicious dress to follow sacrifice—the error is very great.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Personnel rule on public removal after burial applied only to zhou mourning and below; later practice wrongly extended it to three-year parental mourning—a grave error.

sentences.zh: 又據律文：『諸廟享，有緦麻以上喪，不許執事，祭天地、社稷不禁。』

translations.literal: Again according to the code text: 'For all temple offerings, those with si-ma and above mourning may not preside; sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain is not forbidden.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited law forbidding si-ma mourning or above from presiding at temple rites but not at Heaven, Earth, or soil-and-grain sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 此唐之定律者不詳經典意也。

translations.literal: This Tang law-maker did not understand the canonical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That Tang statute, he argued, misunderstood the classics.

sentences.zh: 《王制》曰：『喪三年不祭，惟天地、社稷為越紼而行事。』

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations says: 'Mourning three years without sacrifice—only for Heaven and Earth and the altars of soil and grain does one cross the mourning cord to perform the rite.'
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations states that during three-year mourning only Heaven, Earth, and soil-and-grain rites may be performed by crossing the mourning cord.

sentences.zh: 《注》云：『不敢以卑廢尊也。』

translations.literal: Commentary says: 'Not daring to use the lowly to abandon the honored.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains this means the ruler must not let private mourning cancel rites to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 是指王者不敢以私親之喪，廢天地、社 稷之祭，非謂臣下有父母喪，而得從天子祭天地、社稷也。

translations.literal: This refers to the king not daring to use private kin mourning to abandon Heaven, Earth, and soil-and-grain sacrifice—not meaning that subjects with parents' mourning may follow the Son of Heaven in sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: That passage concerns the ruler's duty not to cancel Heaven and Earth rites for private mourning—not permission for mourning subjects to join the emperor's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 兼律文所以不禁者，亦止謂緦麻以上、周以下故也。

translations.literal: Moreover why the code text does not forbid—it also only refers to si-ma and above, zhou and below.
translations.idiomatic: The law's exception likewise applied only to si-ma through zhou mourning, not three-year parental mourning.

sentences.zh: 南郊、太廟，俱為吉祀，奉承之意，無容異禮。

translations.literal: Southern Suburbs and the Grand Temple are both auspicious sacrifices; the intent of reverent service admits no differing ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Suburban and Grand Temple rites are equally auspicious; reverence toward the state admits no double standard.

sentences.zh: 今居 父母喪不得入太廟，至南郊則為愈重。

translations.literal: Now dwelling in parents' mourning one may not enter the Grand Temple, yet reaching the Southern Suburbs is treated as even more weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Barring parental mourners from the Grand Temple while allowing the Southern Suburban rite—which is the greater sacrifice—is inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每因大禮，侍祠之官普有沾賚，使居喪之人得預祠事，是不欲慶澤之行，有所不被，奈何以小惠而傷大禮？

translations.literal: The court every time because of great ritual, attending-sacrifice officials universally receive bestowed gifts—allowing those dwelling in mourning to participate in sacrificial affairs—is not wishing that the progress of celebratory grace should have any not covered; how can one use small favor to harm great ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Court rewards at grand rites tempt mourning officials to participate so no one misses imperial grace—but trading small favor for great ritual propriety is wrong.

sentences.zh: 近歲兩製以 上，並許終喪，惟於武臣尚仍舊制，是亦取古之墨縗從事，金革無避之義也。

translations.literal: In recent years both civil and military ranks and above are all permitted to complete mourning; only for military officers the old regulation still applies—this also takes the ancient meaning of ink-sashed engagement, war-and-armor without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Recently both civil and military senior officials may complete mourning; only military officers follow the old rule, invoking the ancient principle of mourning in battle dress when war forbids delay.

sentences.zh: 然於郊祀吉禮則為不可。」

translations.literal: Yet for suburban sacrifice auspicious ritual it is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Yet participation in auspicious suburban sacrifice remains improper."

sentences.zh: 下禮院，議曰：「郊祀大禮，國之重事，百司聯職，僅取齊 集。

translations.literal: It was sent down to the Ritual Court; they deliberated: "Suburban sacrifice great ritual is the state's weighty affair; the hundred offices join duties, barely achieving assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Referred to the Ritual Court, they replied: "Suburban sacrifice was a state priority requiring every office represented.

sentences.zh: 若居喪被起之官悉不與事，則或有妨闕。

translations.literal: If officials dwelling in mourning and recalled to service all did not participate, then there might be obstruction and deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Excluding all recalled mourners might leave critical posts unfilled.

sentences.zh: 但不以慘粗之容接於祭次，則亦可行。

translations.literal: But if one does not present coarse mourning appearance at the sacrificial sequence, then it may also be done.
translations.idiomatic: Provided they do not appear in coarse mourning at the rite itself, participation may be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 請依《太常新禮》，宗室及文武官有遭喪被起及卒哭赴朝參者，遇大朝會，聽不 入；

translations.literal: We request following the New Ritual of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: imperial clansmen and civil and military officials who encountered mourning and were recalled, and those who after end of wailing attend court audience—when encountering great court assembly, are permitted not to enter;
translations.idiomatic: Following the New Ritual of Imperial Sacrifices, recalled mourners and those attending court after wailing might skip great assemblies;

sentences.zh: 若緣郊廟大禮，惟不入宗廟，其郊壇、景靈宮得權從吉服陪位，或差攝行事。」

translations.literal: If because of suburban and temple great ritual, only not entering the ancestral temple; at the suburban altar and Jingling Palace they may temporarily follow auspicious dress to accompany in place, or be dispatched as substitute to perform the rite."
translations.idiomatic: but for suburban and temple grand rites they should not enter the ancestral temple; at the suburban altar and Jingling Palace they might attend in regular dress or serve as substitutes."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 天聖五年，侍講學士孫奭言：「伏見禮院及刑法司外州執守 服制，詞旨俚淺，如外祖卑於舅姨，大功加於嫂叔，顛倒謬妄，難可遽言。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiansheng, Lecturing Academician Sun Shi said: "I humbly observe that the Ritual Court and Penal Affairs Office, in outer prefectures enforcing mourning dress regulations—the wording is vulgar and shallow; such as maternal grandfather ranked below maternal uncle and aunt, greater merit added above elder brother's wife and younger brother's wife— inverted and absurd, hard to speak of hastily.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng 5 (1027) Lecturing Academician Sun Shi said: "The Ritual and Penal offices' mourning regulations for outer prefectures were crude and erroneous—ranking maternal grandfathers below uncles and aunts and greater mourning above sisters-in-law—too confused to recount.

sentences.zh: 臣於《開寶正禮》錄出五服年月，並見行喪服制度，編祔《假寧令》，請下兩製、禮院詳 定。」

translations.literal: Your subject from the Correct Ritual of the Kaibao era extracted the years and months of the five degrees of mourning, together with the mourning-garb system currently in force, compiled and appended them to the Leave and Rest Statute, and requests that it be sent down to civil and military officials and the Ritual Court for detailed determination."
translations.idiomatic: I have extracted the five degrees of mourning and their durations from the Correct Ritual of Kaibao, together with the mourning dress now in effect, and appended them to the Leave and Rest Statute. I ask that civil and military officials and the Ritual Court review and fix the text."

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨劉筠等言：「奭所上五服制度，皆應禮經。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Liu Yun and others said: "The five-degrees mourning system submitted by Shi accords throughout with the ritual classics.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Liu Yun and others replied: "Shi's proposed five-degrees mourning code accorded with the ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 然其義簡奧，世俗不能盡通，今解之以就平易。

translations.literal: Yet its meaning is terse and abstruse; common society cannot fully comprehend it. We now explain it to make it plain.
translations.idiomatic: Its wording was too terse and obscure for ordinary readers, so they clarified it in plainer language.

sentences.zh: 若『兩相為服，無所降殺』，舊皆言『服』者，具載 所為服之人；

translations.literal: Where it says 'mutual mourning between two parties, with no reduction of degree,' wherever the old text simply says 'mourning,' they fully record the person for whom mourning is worn;
translations.idiomatic: Where the rule read 'mutual mourning without reduction,' they spelled out exactly who wore mourning for whom whenever the old text had only said 'mourning';

sentences.zh: 其言『周』者，本避唐諱，合復為『期』。

translations.literal: Where it says 'zhou,' this originally avoided the Tang taboo and should be restored to 'qi' (one-year mourning).
translations.idiomatic: They restored 'qi' wherever 'zhou' appeared, since the latter had been used only to avoid a Tang imperial name.

sentences.zh: 又節取《假寧令》附《五服敕》後，以便有司；

translations.literal: They also excerpted the Leave and Rest Statute and appended it after the Five Degrees Edict, for the convenience of the responsible offices;
translations.idiomatic: They also excerpted relevant passages from the Leave and Rest Statute and appended them to the Five Degrees Edict for officials' use;

sentences.zh: 仍板印頒行，而喪服親疏隆殺之紀，始有定制矣。」

translations.literal: and had it block-printed and promulgated. Thus the regulations on mourning dress—near and distant kin, elevated and reduced degrees—at last had fixed standards."
translations.idiomatic: and had the code printed and issued. Mourning dress by kinship rank and degree was at last given a fixed standard."

sentences.zh: 子為嫁母。

translations.literal: A son's mourning for a remarried mother.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for a Remarried Mother

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，禮官宋祁言：「前祠部員外郎、集賢校理郭稹幼孤，母邊更嫁，有子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, Ritual Official Song Qi said: "The former Assistant Director of the Directorate of Sacrifices and Academician Collator Guo Zhen was orphaned young. His mother, Lady Bian, remarried and had other sons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 2 (1035), Ritual Official Song Qi reported: "Guo Zhen, formerly of the Sacrifices Directorate and the Hanlin Academy, had lost his father young. His mother Lady Bian had remarried and borne other children.

sentences.zh: 稹無伯叔兄弟，獨承郭氏之祭。

translations.literal: Zhen had no paternal uncles or brothers and alone inherited the Guo clan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: With no uncles or brothers, Zhen alone maintained the Guo ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 今邊不幸，而稹解宮行服。

translations.literal: Now Lady Bian has died untimely, and Zhen has resigned office to observe mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Bian died, Zhen resigned his post to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 按《五服 制度敕》齊衰杖期降服之條曰：『父卒母嫁及出妻之子為母。』

translations.literal: According to the article on reduced qi mourning with staff and one-year period in the Five Degrees Mourning Dress Edict: 'When the father has died and the mother remarries, and the son of a divorced wife for his mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi cited the Five Degrees Edict on reduced qi mourning with staff: 'When the father is dead and the mother remarries, or when the son of a divorced wife mourns his mother—'

sentences.zh: 其左方注：『謂不為父後者。

translations.literal: The note in the left margin: 'Refers to one who is not the heir to carry on the father's line.
translations.idiomatic: The marginal note read: 'This applies only to one who is not the heir.'

sentences.zh: 若為父後者，則為嫁母無服。』詔議之。」

translations.literal: If one is the heir to the father's line, then for a remarried mother there is no mourning dress.' An edict ordered deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: An heir, by contrast, wore no mourning for a remarried mother. The court ordered deliberation."

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉夔曰：

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Liu Kui said:
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Liu Kui argued:

sentences.zh: 按天聖六年敕，《開元五服制度》、《開寶正禮》並載齊衰降服條例，雖與祁言不異，然《假寧令》：「諸喪，斬、齊三年，並解官；

translations.literal: According to the edict of the sixth year of Tiansheng, the Kaiyuan Five Degrees Mourning System and the Correct Ritual of Kaibao both record provisions on reduced qi mourning—though not different from Qi's words—yet the Leave and Rest Statute: 'For all mourning, zhan and qi of three years, all resign office;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui cited the Tiansheng 6 edict, the Kaiyuan Five Degrees code, and the Correct Ritual of Kaibao, which matched Song Qi on reduced qi mourning. But the Leave and Rest Statute required: "All zhan and qi mourning of three years requires resignation from office;

sentences.zh: 齊衰杖期及為人後者為其父 母，若庶子為後為其母，亦解官，申心喪；

translations.literal: qi mourning with staff and one-year period, and an heir for his father and mother, and if a common-born son as heir for his mother, also resign office and declare inner mourning;
translations.idiomatic: it also required resignation and declaration of inner mourning for one-year qi mourning with staff, for an heir mourning parents, and for a common-born son who had become heir mourning his mother;

sentences.zh: 母出及嫁，為父後者雖不服，亦申心喪。」

translations.literal: When the mother is divorced or remarried, though the heir does not wear mourning dress, he still declares inner mourning."
translations.idiomatic: and even when an heir wore no formal mourning for a divorced or remarried mother, he still had to declare inner mourning."

sentences.zh: 《注》云：「皆為生己者。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: "All refer to those who bore one."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explained: "These rules concern only the mother who bore the mourner."

sentences.zh: 《律疏》云：「心喪者，為妾子及出妻之子合降 其服，二十五月內為心喪。」

translations.literal: The Penal Code Commentary says: "Inner mourning: for a concubine's son and the son of a divorced wife, together reducing their mourning dress, observe inner mourning within twenty-five months."
translations.idiomatic: The Penal Code Commentary defined inner mourning: "For concubines' sons and sons of divorced wives, dress is reduced and inner mourning is observed within twenty-five months."

sentences.zh: 再詳格令：「子為嫁母，雖為父後者不服，亦當申心喪。」

translations.literal: Examining the statutes again: "A son for a remarried mother—even though the heir does not wear mourning dress—should still declare inner mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Further statutes held: "A son mourning a remarried mother, even as heir without formal dress, must still declare inner mourning."

sentences.zh: 又稱：「居心喪者，釋服從吉及忘哀作樂、冒哀求仕者，並同父母正服。」

translations.literal: It also states: "Those dwelling in inner mourning who release dress for auspicious occasions, forget grief and make music, or presumptuously beg to take office—all are treated the same as full mourning for parents."
translations.idiomatic: Violations during inner mourning—prematurely resuming normal dress, making music, or seeking office—were punished as severely as breaches of full parental mourning, the code stated: "Those dwelling in inner mourning who release dress for auspicious occasions, forget grief and make music, or presumptuously beg to take office are treated the same as full mourning for parents."

sentences.zh: 今龍圖閣學士王博文、御史中丞杜衍嘗為出嫁母解官行喪。

translations.literal: Now Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Wang Bowen and Censor-in-Chief Du Yan once resigned office to observe mourning for a mother who had married out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bowen of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Censor-in-Chief Du Yan had both resigned to mourn mothers who had remarried after their fathers' deaths.

sentences.zh: 若使生為母子，沒為路人，則必虧損名教，上玷孝治。

translations.literal: If while alive they were mother and son yet after death became strangers, this would necessarily damage name and teaching and above stain the governance of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: To treat them as strangers in death after a lifetime as mother and son would violate moral teaching and tarnish the dynasty's claim to rule by filial virtue.

sentences.zh: 且杖期降服之制，本出《開元禮》 文，逮乎天寶降敕，俾終三年，然則當時已悟失禮。

translations.literal: Moreover the system of staff-period reduced mourning originally came from the text of the Kaiyuan Ritual; by the Tianbao descending edict it was made a full three years—thus even then they already perceived a breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The staff-period reduced mourning rule came from the Kaiyuan Ritual, but a Tianbao edict had extended it to three years—showing that the Tang court itself had already recognized the error.

sentences.zh: 晉袁準謂：「為人後，猶服嫁母。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhun of Jin said: "Though one is another's heir, one still wears mourning for a remarried mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhun of Jin held: "Even an heir should mourn a remarried mother.

sentences.zh: 據外祖異族，猶廢祭行服，知父後應服嫁母。」

translations.literal: Citing the maternal grandfather as a different clan—yet still suspending sacrifice and wearing mourning—one knows the heir should wear mourning for a remarried mother."
translations.idiomatic: If mourning was worn and sacrifice suspended even for a maternal grandfather of another clan, an heir ought all the more to mourn a remarried mother."

sentences.zh: 劉智釋云：「雖為父後，猶為 嫁母齊衰。」

translations.literal: Liu Zhi's commentary says: "Though one is heir to the father's line, one still wears qi mourning for a remarried mother."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi's commentary likewise held: "Though one is heir to the father's line, one still wears qi mourning for a remarried mother."

sentences.zh: 譙周云：「非父所絕，為之服周可也。」

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou said: "If the father did not disown her, wearing one-year mourning for her is acceptable."
